title: What Do Co-Folding Models Learn? Insights from Enhanced Transition Path Sampling
abstract: arXiv:2611.30062v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Co-folding models are diffusion-based generative models that sample biomolecular complexes from distributions learned on a large corpus of experimental data. Although these models are powerful for structure prediction, it remains unclear whether the conformational ensembles they learn resemble physically meaningful statistical ensembles. To understand what these models learn, we introduce transition path sampling (TPS), which uses Markov chain Monte Carlo over denoising trajectories to sample the learned distribution. Because its Monte Carlo trajectories resemble biomolecular dynamics, TPS couples directly with enhanced-sampling techniques to recover the full conformational ensemble. Applied to Boltz-2, enhanced TPS reveals physical conformational changes biased toward crystal-like states near the training data, indicating both learned physics and memorization. These results suggest new ways to evaluate and improve co-folding models by

translated_title: 共折叠模型学到了什么？来自增强过渡路径采样的洞见
translated_abstract: 共折叠模型是基于扩散的生成模型，它们从在大量实验数据语料库上学习到的分布中采样生物分子复合物。尽管这些模型在结构预测方面非常强大，但它们学习到的构象系综是否类似于具有物理意义的统计系综仍不清楚。为了理解这些模型学到了什么，我们引入了过渡路径采样（TPS），该方法在去噪轨迹上使用马尔可夫链蒙特卡洛来对学习到的分布进行采样。由于其蒙特卡洛轨迹类似于生物分子动力学，TPS 可直接与增强采样技术耦合，从而恢复完整的构象系综。应用于 Boltz-2 时，增强 TPS 揭示了偏向训练数据附近类晶体状态的物理构象变化，表明模型既学到了物理规律，也存在记忆化现象。这些结果为评估和改进共折叠模型提供了新的途径。
tldr: 本文提出将增强过渡路径采样（TPS）与共折叠模型结合以恢复其完整构象系综，并通过对 Boltz-2 的分析发现模型既学习到了真实的物理构象变化，又表现出对训练数据中类晶体态的记忆。
